title: Independent reading: 1 Corinthians 1:18–31
subtitle: Read contrast and quotation in a polemical argument.
overview: Paul’s argument repeatedly contrasts wisdom and folly, those being saved and those perishing, human boasting and divine action. Mark paired terms and quotations.
Do not treat rhetorical contrast as merely vocabulary; follow which claim each γάρ, ἀλλά, and ἵνα clause supports.

items.grc: ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῖς μὲν ἀπολλυμένοις μωρία ἐστίν.
items.en: For the word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing.

items.grc: τοῖς δὲ σῳζομένοις ἡμῖν δύναμις θεοῦ ἐστιν.
items.en: But to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
